title: Mode
description: The manifest of a mode, mode.yaml at the root of its folder.

name.description: The mode's name; the same as the name of its folder.

description.description: One sentence on what the mode does.

requires.description: What the mode needs from other modes.

interfaces.description: The interfaces whose actions this mode calls; the project config binds each to a mode.

implements.description: The interfaces this mode serves; it must have every action of each, with the same signature.

extraFiles.description: Files at the top of the mode folder beyond the layout's own, such as a tool's configuration or a practices file; the layout check accepts these and no others.

resources.description: Everything a run of this mode may use; anything not declared here is denied.

actions.description: The mode's actions, by kebab-case name.

settings.description: The JSON Schema file of the mode's settings, which the project config gives under settings.

workflows.description: Workflow files of this mode, relative to its folder.

name.description: Kebab-case, starting with a letter; not constructor, a name every JavaScript object has.

interfaceReference.description: An interface name and its major version, as name@major, for example items-store@1.

relativePath.description: A path relative to the mode's folder that neither starts with / nor contains a .. segment.

listedCommand.description: A command a mode lists: the words it runs and the effects it can have.

run.description: The command's fixed words, separated by spaces. When the mode gives commandsStartWith, they follow those words; otherwise the first word is the program. A script names the command and gives only the arguments that come after.

effects.description: Every effect the command can have, at least one; an action may run the command only if it declares each of them.

effect.description: A kind of effect an action may have.

keeping.description: How the kernel keeps a value in its database: as-text, or kept-packed, gzipped and in base64.

budget.description: Limits for a run; every nested call draws from the same budget.

items.description: The most items the run may handle.

usd.description: The most US dollars the run may spend.

tokens.description: The most model tokens the run may use.

minutes.description: The most minutes the run may take.

migrations.description: The folder of SQL migrations, relative to the mode's folder.

files.description: Project paths the mode may read and write, and the folders it keeps throwaway folders in.

throwaway.description: Folders in which the kernel makes folders and links and removes files and folders for the mode. The mode's scripts never read or write files there; its commands fill them.

secrets.description: Names of the secrets the mode may fetch.

network.description: Hosts the mode may reach over HTTPS.

commandsStartWith.description: The words every command the mode lists starts with, separated by spaces, such as the program and the options each command needs. A command runs these words, then the words of its run, then the arguments a script gives. A mode gives them only with commands. A mode outside the kit's components/base/ is granted its commands only when the owner trusts its list.

commands.description: Commands the mode's scripts and skill steps may run, each under a kebab-case name of the mode's own that says what the command is for. A mode outside the kit's components/base/ is granted them only when the owner trusts its list. The effects of a command are the mode author's claim of what it can do: the kernel believes them and cannot check them, and bay check shows each command and its effects to the owner.

action.description: An action: typed input and output, declared effects and the steps that run it.

description.description: One sentence saying when an owner or a mode would use the action.

input.description: The JSON Schema file of the action's input. Left out when an interface the mode implements names the action, since the interface gives it.

output.description: The JSON Schema file of the action's output. Left out when an interface the mode implements names the action, since the interface gives it.

effects.description: Every effect the action may have, including those of the actions it calls.

run.description: The steps of the action, in order.

undo.description: The action of this mode that reverses this one.

budget.description: Limits for a run of this action.

skillOutput.description: How the kernel keeps the output of the action's skill. as-text, as when left out: in its database as text, shown by bay runs. kept-packed: compressed, so no line of it is in any file as text; bay runs says it is kept packed and never prints it; the kernel unpacks it only for the script that called the action, and for the skill's own checks. A kept-packed action's run is one skill step and nothing more, and only a script may call it.

calledOutputs.description: How the kernel keeps every call made under the action: the calls its scripts make, and the calls those make, at any depth. as-text, as when left out: as each called action says. kept-packed: each such call's input, output and reason, and every step under it, are compressed, so no line of them is in any file as text; bay runs says they are kept packed and never prints them; the kernel unpacks them only for the script that made the call and for the skill checks under it. When a script or a skill under it fails, the calling script is told which one failed and not its reason, and a schema's problems there are counted, not quoted. The action's own steps and output are kept as text, and its run has no call step.

scriptTimeLimitSeconds.description: How long each script step in run may take, in whole seconds, at most 1800; left out, 480. When it passes, the kernel stops the script and the run fails. The run's budget of minutes still applies: when fewer minutes are left, the script is stopped when they run out.

step.description: One step of an action: a script, a skill or a call to an action of a required interface.

skill.description: The skill folder, which holds SKILL.md.

tier.description: How capable a model the skill needs.

checks.description: Scripts that check the output; a failure sends the skill back, three rounds at most.

call.description: The action to call, as interface.action, of an interface this mode requires.
